spec.name: Sidi El Hazmiri Mosque
spec.description: The Sidi El Hazmiri Mosque is one of the largest and most significant places of worship in the medina of Ksar el-Kebir. It was originally established as a Zaouiya (Sufi lodge) for the saint Abu Zaid El Hazmiri before being converted into a mosque in the 14th century. The mosque is known for its spacious prayer hall and its role as a major religious landmark in the city's historic center.

timeline.title: Conversion
timeline.description: Conversion of the original Zaouiya into a public mosque.

timeline.title: Renovation
timeline.description: Extensive renovation and reopening of the mosque for daily prayers.

comments: The mosque is a central landmark in the medina's layout.
